newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Two-thirds of Singaporeans work long hours - report.
newsitem.headline: Two-thirds of Singaporeans work long hours - report.

text.p: Two-thirds of Singaporeans work at least five and a half days a week, although a shorter work week is becoming popular, a survey by the Labour Ministry said.
Only 35 percent of all employees in 1996 were on a five-day work week, according to the Labour Ministry report on Conditions of Employment.
About 22 percent of workers "were on the conventional 5-1/2 day and 20 percent on a six-day work week," the report added.

The survey covered 4,600 companies in the private sector with at least 25 employees each and it said the average working hours of Singaporeans increased slightly in 1996 to 43.2 hours against 43 hours reported in 1990.
But the number of those entitled to 15 days annual leave rose to 32 percent in 1996 from 27 percent in 1990.
"The construction sector had the highest proportion of employees (95 percent) with less than 15 days leave due to the predominance of of foreign workers in the sector," the report said.
While some 99 percent of private sector employees received medical benefits, only 11 percent of those surveyed enjoyed housing benefits.
